header_summary:
A new standard has been proposed to embed English BIP39 mnemonics and optional passphrases directly into wallet script descriptors, facilitating seamless mnemonic-based wallet recovery and enhancing interoperability among wallet software. This approach allows wallets to derive BIP32 master keys and support complex key expressions within a single descriptor, streamlining recovery and import processes. Full details and an implementation for Bitcoin Core are available for review and testing at the [pull request](https://github.com/polespinasa/bips/pull/2) and [repository](https://github.com/polespinasa/bitcoin/pull/8).

Within the Elements project, a Hybrid Key Encapsulation (HKE) method has been introduced, combining secp256k1 ECDH and ML-KEM-768 cryptography through a UG combiner function as outlined in [draft-irtf-cfrg-hybrid-kems-12](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-hybrid-kems-12/), ensuring post-quantum security and resistance to chosen ciphertext attacks. This hybrid construction enables robust key encapsulation while maintaining compatibility with existing cryptographic standards ([ELIP pull request](https://github.com/ElementsProject/ELIPs/pull/46)).

Zenul Abidin et al. released spscand, a privacy-focused, watch-only scanner for BIP352 Silent Payments, offering comprehensive output detection, spend tracking, and blockchain reorganization monitoring, with results accessible via local APIs and webhooks. The tool, integrated with libspscan and supporting multiple block sources—including Bitcoin Core, BlindBit Oracle, and BIP158 filters—proactively safeguards user privacy and is available open source at [ZenulAbidin/spscand](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand).

A post-quantum garbled-circuit verifier for hash-based STARK proofs has been developed for BitVM3-style bridges, leveraging the binary field $\mathbb{F}_{2^{128}}$ and Blake3 to ensure efficient, pairing-free verification. This system delivers reduced gate counts and storage requirements compared to previous approaches, as detailed in [“Toward Efficient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges”](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2877) and [bitcoin-stark-verifier](https://github.com/GOATNetwork/bitcoin-stark-verifier).

Recent security analyses uncovered a Lightning Network denial-of-service vulnerability involving channel closure logic, where attackers could trigger persistent crash loops by exploiting channel ID collisions. Ongoing improvements to the smite testing tool are addressing previous detection gaps, and most implementations now appear to handle these vulnerabilities correctly ([pull request](https://github.com/lnfuzz/smite/pull/257)).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] bip39() Descriptor Key Expression
recent_posts.summary:
- A new standard proposes embedding mnemonics and passphrases directly into output script descriptors.
- This enables wallets to securely manage various key expressions and complex derivation setups.
- Draft details, implementation links, and feedback options are provided for review and testing.

recent_posts.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
recent_posts.summary: - A proposal introduces Hybrid Key Encapsulation for Elements, utilizing a UG combiner function.  - Two cryptographic paths, secp256k1 ECDH and ML-KEM-768, are integrated using this function.  - Security against chosen ciphertext attacks is ensured if at least one path remains secure.

recent_posts.title: spscand and libspscan: a watch-only BIP352 scanner
recent_posts.summary: - spscand detects and tracks BIP352 silent payment outputs with strong privacy protections and flexible block sources.  - libspscan, a C library, handles BIP352 receiving logic and cryptographic operations, ensuring minimal integration dependencies.  - Performance is efficient across methods, with comprehensive tests confirming accuracy, privacy, and correct network behavior.

recent_posts.title: Toward Efficient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges
recent_posts.summary: - A garbled-circuit verifier for hash-based STARK proofs offers a post-quantum alternative for Bitcoin bridges.  - Efficiency is achieved through binary fields, consistent use of Blake3, and optimized input minimization strategies.  - The solution outperforms alternatives, with smaller garbled tables and lower on-chain and storage costs.

recent_posts.title: Silent Payments for Electrum
recent_posts.summary:
- A new open source tool, spscand, enhances Silent Payments monitoring and integrates with an existing plugin.
- The tool privately scans sp1 addresses, supports Tor, and offers flexible notifications via API and webhooks.
- Users benefit from a secure, privacy-focused toolkit for sending and tracking Silent Payments transactions.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: DoS vulnerability fixed in Core Lightning v26.06.8
recent_posts.summary: - An exploitable bug allowed costless attacks by sending error messages, causing persistent crash loops.  - The testing tool smite missed this vulnerability due to lacking support for sending error messages.  - Collision between outpoint and channel_id caused significant vulnerabilities, now mostly fixed in implementations.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal enables nodes to share stale tip information to improve stale rate visibility.  - Stale rate awareness helps diagnose issues like network partitions, adversarial mining, and propagation delays.  - Technical design incorporates BIP 434 messages, tip sharing limits, compressed headers, and a recent tips cache.

active_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
active_posts.summary: - A new Bitcoin address format, `bc1z`, uses quantum-resistant ML-DSA-65 signatures and SHA-256 commitments.  - The proposal includes a Python implementation, signature compression techniques, and maintains backward compatibility via soft fork.  - Community feedback is sought on security, migration strategies, and timing of adoption before quantum threats arise.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Transport Feature Negotiation
active_posts.summary: - The protocol introduces structured negotiation of transport features like encryption and authentication for Bitcoin nodes.  - It uses a repurposed "version packet" to exchange feature lists and enforce mutual compatibility during handshake.  - The design allows future feature expansion, streamlines negotiation, and considers staggered negotiation for enhanced security.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal recommends fixes for Bitcoin's vulnerabilities, including timewarp and Merkle root issues.  - Improvements such as limiting legacy transactions and standardizing technical elements are proposed for security.  - Some suggestions, like reducing block size, are debated due to concerns about scalability and functionality.

active_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
active_posts.summary: - Integrating k-of-n multisig in Lightning Network enhances security, but current protocol limitations hinder direct implementation.  - Proposed BOLT protocol changes would introduce features supporting multisig and improve compatibility across node types.  - Sole reliance on hardware security is insufficient; robust multisig validation offers significantly better fund protection.

active_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
active_posts.summary: - Luke Carriere proposes a policy format to standardize co-signer conditions, enhancing interoperability between technologies.  - The draft introduces open, blinded, and enclave verification to ensure transparent and secure co-signing processes.  - Feedback is requested on representation formats, blinded verification, DLC attestations, output language, and fallback path timelocks.

today_in_history_posts.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Proposed sighash enhancements improve fee transparency and prevent devices from being deceived about output types.  - Optional commitments and new flags, including SIGHASH_NOINPUT, SIGHASH_NOFEE, and SIGHASH_SCRIPTMASK, allow flexible transaction security.  - The approach aims for a balance between security, explicit commitments, and adaptability to various transaction needs.

today_in_history_posts.title: [PATCH] First draft of option_simplfied_commitment
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Channel management employs fee negotiation, unique keys, and per-commitment secrets for enhanced security.  - Specific commitment and HTLC transactions employ separate key structures and change processes to prevent transaction guessing.  - Fee updates and channel reserves follow strict conditions and `option_simplified_commitment` influences fee update requirements.

today_in_history_posts.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The analysis explores how block propagation times impact miner revenue and encourage centralization.  - Simulations reveal that even slight propagation differences significantly affect stale rates and mining rewards.  - Reducing network delays could promote fairness and decentralization among miners of varying pool sizes.
